static_traits.name: Li Bowen
static_traits.social_status: Lacking social support to confide in
static_traits.medical_history: Denying major physical illness; never received psychotherapy in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to reflect, good cooperativeness, neutral tone

basic_info.main_problem: I constantly think 'as long as I watch my diet, I will never get to eat delicious food again'; these thoughts bring a sense of deprivation and frustration, and almost every meal is accompanied by guilt and anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: I want to stop feeling guilty and anxious about food, and be able to enjoy meals without pressure.

core_beliefs: If I cannot perfectly stick to a healthy diet, I am just a failure

special_situations.event: Every time sitting down to eat
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by completely avoiding 'delicious' or high-calorie foods can a healthy diet be maintained
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strictly restricts diet, preferentially chooses options considered 'healthy', avoids tempting foods
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I eat delicious food, I will lose control and be unable to maintain a healthy diet

special_situations.event: When strong cravings for delicious food arise
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once there is one indulgence, one will completely lose control and all prior effort will be wasted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repressing cravings, reducing contact with tempting foods or situations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I indulge even a little, I will completely lose control

special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Blames oneself and afterward adopts a stricter restrictive diet to make up for it
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed; all previous effort was wasted

special_situations.event: When deciding to focus on healthy eating and making choices in daily meals
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: For the sake of health, I will never enjoy delicious food again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Restricting diet in extreme ways, giving myself no 'exceptions'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never get to eat delicious food again

exception_events.target_problem: After occasionally eating delicious food, the client usually feels like a failure and worries about losing control over diet, then falls into guilt and anxiety.
exception_events.unique_outcome: After eating delicious food several times, the client did not stay out of control, but was able to return to a healthy eating routine.
exception_events.reason: Clue: the client has experience of self-regulation, having restored the established eating rhythm through self-management after indulgence.

positive_force: Has experience of returning to healthy eating after indulgence (self-regulation ability)
Actively seeks psychological counseling to improve his relationship with food
Able to reflect and willing to try recording successful experiences
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and predicting the future
Frequent guilt and anxiety experiences during meals
Lacking social support to confide in

target_behavior.behavior: Strong guilt and anxiety during meals, accompanied by overly restrictive eating
antecedent: Each time sitting down to eat
When cravings for delicious food arise
target_behavior.core_reason: Influenced by black-and-white thinking, catastrophizing, and predicting the future, forming the belief that 'indulging once means completely losing control; enjoyment and health cannot coexist'
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the consequences of being seen as 'unhealthy' and 'out of control', seeking a sense of safety and control over diet
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased mealtime pleasure, increased stress, daily life affected, finding it hard to enjoy food and harming mental health
